name: Dead Can Dance
label: 4AD
lede: Two Melbourne post-punks moved to London, dropped the guitars for cello, hurdy-gurdy and a Chinese hammered dulcimer, and became the biggest-selling act on 4AD. Lisa Gerrard sang in a language she made up; Brendan Perry built a studio in an Irish church.

eras.title: Melbourne, then London
eras.text: Brendan Perry had been a New Zealand punk called Ronnie Recent; Lisa Gerrard had grown up in Prahran with Greek music coming through the walls. They met in Melbourne's Little Band scene, headlined the Crystal Ballroom, and left for London within a year.

years.src: Wikipedia: Dead Can Dance · Wikipedia: Brendan Perry · Wikipedia: Lisa Gerrard
years.h: Perry starts a trio, and Gerrard joins it
years.p: [[Brendan Perry|406fa1ec-0f9f-47ac-b2a3-52eccf987af6]] forms Dead Can Dance in Melbourne with Paul Erikson on bass and Simon Monroe of the Marching Girls on drums. [[Lisa Gerrard|cd645207-1664-46af-9953-264e9ae54089]], from the post-punk band Microfilm, joins on vocals and percussion.
years.xp:
Perry was born in Whitechapel, London, moved to Auckland at 14, and sang in the punk band the Scavengers as Ronnie Recent. They moved to Melbourne in 1978 and became the Marching Girls; Perry left in 1980 to work with tape loops and synthesizers.

Gerrard grew up with Irish parents in Prahran, a suburb with a big Greek community. She remembered 'Mediterranean music blaring out of the houses'.

years.h: The first release is on a cassette magazine
years.p: A home recording of 'Fatal Impact' appears in the December issue of Fast Forward.

years.cap: Lisa Gerrard, Paul Erikson and Peter Ulrich rehearsing on the Isle of Dogs, London
years.h: A farewell show at the Crystal Ballroom, then London
years.p: The band had become headliners at the St Kilda post-punk venue. After the last Australian show they move to London, where Peter Ulrich takes over on drums.

eras.title: Out of the goth crowd
eras.text: 4AD signed them on arrival, and the first record sounded like the label's other dark bands. Then they threw out the guitars, Gerrard sang on This Mortal Coil, and Spleen and Ideal sounded like it came from a cathedral.

years.h: Two weeks at Blackwing, then a third they asked for
years.p: [[Ivo Watts-Russell|cf86cec1-1baf-4d8a-ba1e-01568332585a]] gives the band two weeks to make a debut; they talk him into a third. Perry hated how it came out.
years.xp: 'We didn't get on with [engineer John Fryer] at all,' Perry said. The result was 'swamped with reverb', and to him it sounded 'overprocessed and kind of thin-sounding'.

years.src: Wikipedia: Dead Can Dance (album) · Wikipedia: Dead Can Dance
years.h: Dead Can Dance, behind a mask from New Guinea
years.p: Perry designs the cover: a Papua New Guinea mask beside the band's name in Greek-looking letters. AllMusic later calls it 'a striking, dour landmark'.

years.h: Garden of the Arcane Delights widens the palette
years.p: A four-track EP reaching into a wider range of music, from a band that never accepted the goth label.

years.cap: Peter Ulrich and Lisa Gerrard live in The Hague, 1984
years.h: Gerrard sings on This Mortal Coil's It'll End in Tears
years.p: On Watts-Russell's 4AD supergroup album, Gerrard writes and sings 'Waves Become Wings' and 'Dreams Made Flesh'. Perry plays a bass drone.
years.xp: The same record carries [[Elizabeth Fraser|0bf0cabe-def2-4113-8dc5-6e721b9c3a92]] and [[Robin Guthrie|47d7b25e-585b-4c97-b98b-411b21a53379]]'s 'Song to the Siren', which spent two years on the UK independent chart. [[This Mortal Coil|60ef8ddb-7676-4056-a357-9a8c228d03a6]] made 4AD a sound as much as a label.

years.src: Wikipedia: Spleen and Ideal · Wikipedia: Dead Can Dance
years.h: Spleen and Ideal trades guitars for cello, trombone and timpani
years.p: Named from Baudelaire's Les Fleurs du mal and made at Woodbine in Warwickshire with John A. Rivers. It reaches No. 2 on the UK indie chart.
years.xp: The sound was medieval and churchy, 'like it was recorded in an immense cathedral', as the band's Wikipedia history puts it. The cover shows a grain elevator being demolished at Salford Quays.

eras.title: A council flat on the Isle of Dogs
eras.text: Three albums in four years, each one reaching further back in time. The couple at the centre split up in 1989 and moved to different countries, and the band carried on anyway.

years.h: Within the Realm of a Dying Sun: his side, then hers
years.p: Perry sings the first half, Gerrard the second, including 'Cantara'. The cover is the Raspail family tomb at Père Lachaise in Paris.
years.xp: 'We realised we had been limiting our musical visions,' the band said, 'relying around guitar, bass and drums.'
play: Within the Realm of a Dying Sun

years.h: The Serpent's Egg is made mostly in a council flat
years.p: Recorded on the Isle of Dogs in London while Perry and Gerrard are still a couple. Its opener, 'The Host of Seraphim', ends up in Baraka, The Mist and a Terminator 3 trailer.
years.xp: AllMusic called 'The Host of Seraphim' 'so jaw-droppingly good that almost the only reaction is sheer awe'. 'Severance' later got a cover from [[Bauhaus|0688add2-c282-4ee2-ba61-223ffdb3c201]], on their 1999 live album Gotham.

years.cap: Brendan Perry and Lisa Gerrard in London, 1989
years.h: Perry and Gerrard split up, and keep the band
years.p: Gerrard moves to Barcelona and then home to Australia; Perry settles in Ireland. They go on writing, recording and touring as Dead Can Dance.

years.h: Aion puts Bosch on the cover and a saltarello inside
years.p: Recorded at Perry's new studio in Quivvy Church, Ireland. It mixes originals with a 14th-century Italian dance and a 16th-century Catalan ballad, played on hurdy-gurdy and viols.
years.xp: The cover is a detail from the central panel of Hieronymus Bosch's The Garden of Earthly Delights. Male soprano David Navarro Sust sings on two tracks.

eras.title: 4AD's biggest seller
eras.text: Recorded by two people on two continents, Into the Labyrinth sold half a million copies and made Dead Can Dance the best-selling act on Ivo Watts-Russell's label. They toured the world, made one more album, and split during the next one.

years.src: Wikipedia: Into the Labyrinth · Wikipedia: Dead Can Dance
years.h: Two people on two continents make Into the Labyrinth
years.p: The first album with no guest players, recorded at Quivvy while Perry lives on an Irish river island and Gerrard in Australia. It sells more than 500,000 copies and reaches the Billboard 200.
years.xp: 'Yulunga' takes its name from a Gamilaraay word for dance. Perry called 'The Ubiquitous Mr Lovegrove' his alter ego, and 'The Carnival Is Over' came from childhood memories of circuses in East London.

years.h: The world tour, filmed as Toward the Within
years.p: A show recorded in California comes out as a live album and on laserdisc and VHS.

q: I believed that I was speaking to God when I sang in that language.
years.h: Gerrard's first solo album, The Mirror Pool
years.p: Her voice on its own, often in an invented language she said she'd had 'for a very long time'.

years.h: George Harrison gets a co-write on Spiritchaser
years.p: 'Indus' borrows the melody of the Beatles' 'Within You Without You'. Harrison gives permission; the label insists on a credit. The album tops the US World Albums chart.
years.xp: It reached No. 75 on the Billboard 200. Max Cavalera later named it his favourite non-metal album.

years.h: The band splits in the middle of the next album
years.p: A follow-up to Spiritchaser and a world tour were planned for 1999. Both are cancelled; one song, 'The Lotus Eaters', comes out later on a box set and the 2003 compilation Wake.

eras.title: Gladiator, and a Golden Globe
eras.text: Apart, the two went in very different directions: Perry made a solo album, and Gerrard's voice went into Hollywood films.

years.src: Wikipedia: Dead Can Dance · Wikipedia: Brendan Perry
years.h: Perry's Eye of the Hunter
years.p: His first solo album, after Gerrard's 1998 Duality with Pieter Bourke.

years.h: Gerrard and Hans Zimmer score Gladiator
years.p: After Michael Mann's The Insider, she co-writes Ridley Scott's epic with Hans Zimmer. The score wins the Golden Globe and is nominated for an Oscar.
years.xp: Film work became a second career: Whale Rider, Ali and many more. Gerrard also plays the yangqin, a Chinese hammered dulcimer, across her records.

eras.title: Anastasis means resurrection
eras.text: A reunion tour, then a long quiet, then a forum post. Two more albums followed, on PIAS rather than 4AD, and the tours reached Turkey, Lebanon and South America.

years.cap: The reunion tour in Munich, March 27, 2005
years.h: The first reunion tour sells its own recordings
years.p: Thirteen European and eight North American shows are released as limited live recordings. In Mexico, 'Nierika' opens the soap opera La Chacala.

years.cap: Cemil Topuzlu Open-Air Theatre, Istanbul, September 19, 2012
years.src: Wikipedia: Anastasis · Wikipedia: Dead Can Dance
years.h: Anastasis, the first album in 16 years
years.p: Perry announced it on his forum in May 2011. Made at Quivvy and released on PIAS, it reaches No. 46 on the Billboard 200.
years.xp: The title is Greek for resurrection. The world tour ran from August 2012 to July 2013, through Turkey, Greece, Russia, Lebanon, Mexico, South America and Australia, and ended in Santiago, Chile.

years.h: Quivvy Church goes up for sale
years.p: The band cancels a spring 2015 European tour in October 2014 'due to unforeseen circumstances'. The next year, the sale of Perry's church studio is announced.

years.src: Wikipedia: Dionysus · Wikipedia: Dead Can Dance
years.h: Perry and Gerrard split Dionysus into two acts
years.p: Mastered at Abbey Road, the album is indexed on physical copies as just two tracks. The cover is Huichol art from Mexico.

years.h: 'A Celebration: Life & Works 1980–2019' hits Europe
years.p: The career tour runs through May and June, with North and South American legs announced that October.

eras.title: Perry on his own
eras.text: The pandemic wiped out two years of dates. The next tour was cut short, and Gerrard said she was done. Perry kept the name.

years.cap: Lisa Gerrard at the Stadsschouwburg, Antwerp, April 20, 2022
years.h: The rest of the 2022 tour is cancelled
years.p: After a European run, the band calls off a second European leg and the North American dates, citing unspecified health reasons.

years.h: Lisa Gerrard says Dead Can Dance is over
years.p: She points to disagreements during Dionysus and over the last tour's setlists.
years.xp: Gerrard said the shows had started to 'wean itself away from the kind of connection that we had together'.

years.h: Perry makes Apollo as a one-man Dead Can Dance
years.p: Announced in April as a sequel to Dionysus, it's confirmed in May as a Dead Can Dance album with Perry the only musician.

years.h: 'Our Day Will Come', the first new single in five years
years.p: Dedicated to solidarity between the Irish and Palestinian peoples, with half the proceeds to Medical Aid for Palestinians, and sold only on Bandcamp via Holy Tongue Records. 'Death Cults' follows on April 18.
